raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Thanks to @TKONIY for the collaboration on this work.

## Overview

Add opt-in producer-assisted LiteTopK for paged FP8/FP32 decode and verify,
ported from the SGLang decode work. Requires
[DeepGEMM #24](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/24).
This description includes the optimized companion producer measurements;
the vLLM FP32 integration needs no additional code change.

## Claims

- Supports the H32/D128, page64, top2048 SM100-family decode contract for n=1..4.
- Selects exact logical indices with lower-index tie breaking and persistent
  workspace; preserves prefill, explicit backend and unsupported-path fallbacks.
- The updated companion removes repeated varlen histogram flushes for n>1.

## Validation

B200 (148 SMs), Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3, PDL enabled.
Three isolated process blocks per version; nine shuffled CUDA-graph samples per
block. Captured GLM-5.2/DSpark operands use distinct KV replicas totaling at least
256 MiB. Timings include metadata generation/copy once per eight layers and are
reported per layer. They exclude the rest of the model and are not serving
latency. Across all 40 shapes, live logits, exact histograms and logical-index
selection agree between submitted and optimized versions in all 240 cases.
The full grid with ranges, the method and the validation record are below.


| dtype | B | n | context | submitted µs | optimized µs | old/new | default/new |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fp32 | 1 | 4 | 1048320 | 65.637 | 39.280 | 1.671x | 1.565x |
| fp32 | 4 | 4 | 1048320 | 222.181 | 116.323 | 1.910x | 1.511x |

The updated producer suite passed 8 FP32 native/varlen cases, including live
length and request-ID changes during graph replay. The combined route suite
passed 18 cases; the unchanged native selector passed its 30-case suite during
the original migration. Commands:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_litetopk_decode.py -v -s
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_litetopk_decode.py --widths 8192 65536 262144 1048576 --requests 1 4 --repeats 5
```

The repository benchmark is a hot per-layer check and excludes shared metadata.
The table above comes from the metadata-inclusive captured benchmark below. Some 8K shapes remain slower than default.

DeepGEMM was rebuilt from the companion changes. vLLM validation
used current Python source, the separately compiled selector, and unchanged
binaries from `f944491db`; this was not a full exact-base wheel build.
The complete draft-test module is unavailable because the generated FlashMLA
Python interface is missing; the two modified cases and actual metadata builder
were executed through narrow imports. Applicable lint/type checks and clean
patch-application/tree checks passed.

**Model evaluation:** not completed. The available model weights total
510,296,708,312 bytes, more than the single ~179 GiB B200 I had for this.
No output-quality, speculative-acceptance or end-to-end serving gain is claimed.
Full model evaluation remains required before merge.


<details>
<summary>Full FP32 results, method and validation record</summary>

Geometric means over the FP32 grid (B={1,4}, n={1,4}, context {8192, 65536, 262144, 1048320}):

| dtype | cells | submitted / optimized | default / submitted | default / optimized |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fp32 | 16 | 1.164x | 1.128x | 1.311x |

| dtype | B | n | context | submitted µs | optimized µs | old/new | default/new |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fp32 | 1 | 1 | 8192 | 9.926 [9.549, 10.124] | 9.847 [9.748, 10.227] | 1.008x | 0.942x |
| fp32 | 1 | 1 | 65536 | 10.677 [10.090, 10.685] | 10.344 [10.312, 10.824] | 1.032x | 1.668x |
| fp32 | 1 | 1 | 262144 | 15.933 [15.752, 15.952] | 15.956 [15.834, 16.029] | 0.999x | 1.550x |
| fp32 | 1 | 1 | 1048320 | 33.200 [33.031, 33.966] | 33.558 [33.517, 34.007] | 0.989x | 1.780x |
| fp32 | 1 | 4 | 8192 | 10.979 [10.962, 11.270] | 10.864 [10.576, 10.901] | 1.010x | 0.937x |
| fp32 | 1 | 4 | 65536 | 13.783 [13.612, 13.789] | 12.299 [12.059, 12.320] | 1.121x | 1.477x |
| fp32 | 1 | 4 | 262144 | 24.399 [24.222, 24.436] | 18.033 [18.014, 18.108] | 1.353x | 1.455x |
| fp32 | 1 | 4 | 1048320 | 65.637 [65.493, 65.738] | 39.280 [39.071, 39.371] | 1.671x | 1.565x |
| fp32 | 4 | 1 | 8192 | 10.500 [10.456, 10.503] | 10.684 [10.266, 10.685] | 0.983x | 0.955x |
| fp32 | 4 | 1 | 65536 | 16.138 [15.746, 16.165] | 16.189 [15.981, 16.215] | 0.997x | 1.388x |
| fp32 | 4 | 1 | 262144 | 33.238 [33.124, 33.250] | 33.448 [33.443, 33.505] | 0.994x | 1.261x |
| fp32 | 4 | 1 | 1048320 | 97.386 [97.251, 97.565] | 97.854 [97.500, 97.965] | 0.995x | 1.236x |
| fp32 | 4 | 4 | 8192 | 12.228 [12.181, 12.357] | 11.916 [11.851, 11.954] | 1.026x | 0.896x |
| fp32 | 4 | 4 | 65536 | 25.576 [25.447, 25.670] | 19.038 [18.899, 19.088] | 1.343x | 1.350x |
| fp32 | 4 | 4 | 262144 | 66.531 [66.524, 66.761] | 39.587 [39.531, 39.638] | 1.681x | 1.484x |
| fp32 | 4 | 4 | 1048320 | 222.181 [221.879, 222.532] | 116.323 [116.099, 116.555] | 1.910x | 1.511x |

**Method.** One NVIDIA B200 (148 SMs), Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3, PDL enabled; clocks not locked, and the GPU was checked to be idle before each process. Operands are real captures (GLM-5.2 layer 0 FP8, DSpark layer 20 MXFP4); prefix lengths and batches are built from the captured query/weight bank, and KV bytes are copied into separate page sets per request and layer. This repeats one captured layer's operands, not an actual eight-layer model run. Each graph cycles over at least 256 MiB of actively read KV across at least eight layer replicas. The generic split256 metadata plus its copy is timed once per eight layers in every arm; the submitted BF16 version additionally builds split384 metadata and casts weights in every layer, while the optimized version builds and copies split384 metadata once per eight layers (n=1–5 pass FP32 weights, n=6 keeps the BF16 cast). Three fresh process blocks per version with alternating order; within a process, baseline/LiteTopK order is randomized for each of nine samples, each replaying its CUDA graph four times. Values are medians of the three block medians, with [min, max] block medians. Submitted and optimized DeepGEMM run as separate installed packages. Warmup, JIT, host work, operand setup, Q quantization, KV writes, candidate publication, attention and the rest of the model are outside the timed interval. Across the 40 cells, the default chain drifted between package runs by -0.55% to 0.92%.

`old/new` compares the submitted LiteTopK code with the optimized code; `default/new` compares the unchanged FP32-score + auto-selector chain with the optimized LiteTopK chain in the same process. Higher is faster. µs are per layer.

**Checks.**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| DeepGEMM producer suites | 32 passed: FP32 native/varlen n=1..4; BF16 n=1..6, BF16/FP32 weights, PDL off/on |
| Sparse-indexer route suite | 18 passed: reused/per-call schedule, live graph lengths/IDs, explicit backend and candidate fallbacks |
| Metadata builder | compressed, ragged decode with stable-address graph replay passed |
| Draft metadata update | both page64 and page128 modified test cases passed |
| Captured-operand grid | 240 cases passed: bitwise cross-version live logits, histograms and selected-index hashes |
| Weight-path probe | 32 shapes passed: exact histogram/selection checks and direct-vs-cast score equality |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks | Ruff check/format, typos, test tethering, SPDX, lazy/forbidden imports, torch.cuda rules, boolean-context rule, mypy 3.12 |

DeepGEMM's native extension was rebuilt after the host/header changes. On the vLLM side, the current Python source and the separately compiled LiteTopK operator were used with unchanged binaries from `f944491db`; a complete wheel from the exact base was not built. The full draft-metadata test module could not import the generated `vllm.third_party.flashmla.flash_mla_interface` in that environment, so the two modified test functions and the actual builder were run through narrow imports, not full-module pytest. A full all-hook pre-commit run did not complete (actionlint/shellcheck bootstrap), so the applicable hooks were run on every changed file. The captured operands are not redistributable.

</details>

## Details

Enable with `--kernel-config '{"enable_litetopk_decode": true}'`; default is off.
vLLM passes producer histograms to the native selector and shares reusable
workspace across layers. The producer now keeps independent bins for all active
tokens of a varlen Q block, instead of flushing one slot on every token/KV split.
It retains exact per-score counts and handles partial blocks.

**Duplicate-work check:** this updates the existing decode PR and its companion;
[vLLM #48726](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48726) covers prefill.
This adds paged decode/verify integration rather than another prefill PR.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses the existing decode metadata and workspace with opt-in dispatch.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Kernel/route/capture validation passed; full model and serving evaluation remains.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Applicable automated checks passed.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes scope, dependencies, measurements, root cause and limitations.
</details>

files.patch:
@@ -615,6 +615,15 @@ if(VLLM_GPU_LANG STREQUAL "CUDA" OR VLLM_GPU_LANG STREQUAL "HIP")
       CUDA_ARCHS "${MINIMAX_M3_FUSED_ARCHS}")
     list(APPEND VLLM_STABLE_EXT_SRC "${MINIMAX_M3_FUSED_SRC}")
 
+    cuda_archs_loose_intersection(LITETOPK_DECODE_ARCHS
+      "10.0a;10.3a" "${CUDA_ARCHS}")
+    if(LITETOPK_DECODE_ARCHS)
+      list(APPEND VLLM_STABLE_EXT_SRC "csrc/libtorch_stable/litetopk_decode.cu")
+      set_gencode_flags_for_srcs(
+        SRCS "csrc/libtorch_stable/litetopk_decode.cu"
+        CUDA_ARCHS "${LITETOPK_DECODE_ARCHS}")
+    endif()
+
     if(COOPERATIVE_TOPK_ARCHS)
       list(APPEND VLLM_STABLE_EXT_SRC
         "csrc/libtorch_stable/cooperative_topk.cu")
@@ -1239,6 +1248,10 @@ if(VLLM_GPU_LANG STREQUAL "CUDA" OR VLLM_GPU_LANG STREQUAL "HIP")
   # Needed to use cuda/hip APIs from C-shim
   if(VLLM_GPU_LANG STREQUAL "CUDA")
     target_compile_definitions(_C_stable_libtorch PRIVATE USE_CUDA)
+    if(LITETOPK_DECODE_ARCHS)
+      target_compile_definitions(_C_stable_libtorch PRIVATE
+        VLLM_ENABLE_LITETOPK_DECODE=1)
+    endif()
     if(COOPERATIVE_TOPK_ARCHS)
       target_compile_definitions(_C_stable_libtorch PRIVATE
         VLLM_ENABLE_COOPERATIVE_TOPK=1)

@@ -482,6 +482,12 @@ void persistent_topk(const torch::stable::Tensor& logits,
                      int64_t max_seq_len);
 
 #ifdef VLLM_ENABLE_COOPERATIVE_TOPK
+void litetopk_decode(const torch::stable::Tensor& scores,
+                     const torch::stable::Tensor& lengths,
+                     torch::stable::Tensor& histogram,
+                     torch::stable::Tensor& output,
+                     torch::stable::Tensor& workspace, int64_t capacity);
+
 void cooperative_topk(const torch::stable::Tensor& logits,
                       const torch::stable::Tensor& lengths,
                       torch::stable::Tensor& output,

@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+# LiteTopK decode
+
+Enable the experimental producer-assisted path with
+`--kernel-config '{"enable_litetopk_decode": true}'`.
+Build vLLM's CUDA extension and a DeepGEMM companion with
+`paged_mqa_logits_histogram_version >= 1`. An external DeepGEMM installation
+is preferred; source builds can also set `DEEPGEMM_SRC_DIR` to the patched
+DeepGEMM checkout. An unpatched producer falls back to the existing path.
+
+The FP8 route supports SM100, H32/D128, page64, FP32 top2048, and 1..4
+query tokens per request. Prefill, unsupported shapes, context parallelism,
+explicit `sparse_indexer_topk_backend` choices, and candidate mask consumers
+retain the existing dispatch. Candidate sources can publish blocks from the
+unmodified producer scores before selection.
+
+DeepGEMM counts live scores into a coarse histogram while computing logits.
+The CUDA selector refines the crossing bin and writes request-local logical
+indices. Equal ordered score keys prefer lower logical indices; output order
+is unspecified and short rows are padded with -1. This intentionally adapts
+SGLang's physical-slot output and tie rule to vLLM's logical-index contract.
+Candidate overflow or inconsistent counts use an exact whole-row fallback.
+
+Each workspace lane and CUDA stream owns fixed persistent storage, shared
+across layers: 1024 int32 histogram bins, 16 state bytes and 8192 eight-byte
+candidates per maximum token row (about 68 KiB). Profile/warmup reserves this
+storage before the workspace manager locks. Row-count changes do not move the
+candidate region. The selector resets counts/candidates and balances state
+counters for the next layer or CUDA graph replay.
+
+Correctness tests: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k litetopk`.

@@ -2034,3 +2034,68 @@ def decode_kernel(logits, next_n, seq_lens, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
 
     assert recorded["next_n"] == 1
     assert recorded["row_ends"] == [99, 100, 199, 200]
+
+
+def _litetopk_histogram(scores: torch.Tensor, lengths: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    values = scores.float().contiguous()
+    bits = values.view(torch.int32).long() & 0xFFFFFFFF

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Producer-assisted exact decode selection with persistent, reusable storage."""
+
+import functools
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import _import_deep_gemm, _lazy_init
+from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import current_workspace_manager
+
+CANDIDATE_CAPACITY = 8192
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def has_litetopk_decode() -> bool:
+    if (
+        not current_platform.is_cuda()
+        or not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
+    ):
+        return False
+    if not hasattr(torch.ops._C, "litetopk_decode"):
+        return False
+    if not torch._C._dispatch_has_kernel_for_dispatch_key(
+        "_C::litetopk_decode", "CUDA"
+    ):
+        return False
+    _lazy_init()
+    dg = _import_deep_gemm()
+    return getattr(dg, "paged_mqa_logits_histogram_version", 0) >= 1
+
+
+def get_litetopk_workspace(max_rows: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """One fixed allocation per stream and workspace lane, shared across layers.
+
+    States always precede the full candidate region, even for smaller row views.
+    Every successful selection resets its histogram and candidates and balances
+    its state counters, so captured replays need no reset kernel.
+    """
+    manager = current_workspace_manager()
+    key = ("litetopk_decode", torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream)
+    histogram = manager.get_persistent(
+        (key, "histogram"), (max_rows, 1024), torch.int32, zero_init=True
+    )
+    workspace = manager.get_persistent(
+        (key, "workspace"),
+        (max_rows * (16 + CANDIDATE_CAPACITY * 8),),
+        torch.uint8,
+        zero_init=True,
+    )
+    return histogram, workspace
+
+
+def supports_litetopk_decode(q, q_scale, weights, page_size, topk, next_n) -> bool:
+    return (
+        q.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        and q_scale is None
+        and q.shape[1] <= 4
+        and q.shape[2:] == (32, 128)
+        and weights.dtype == torch.float32
+        and page_size == 64
+        and topk == 2048
+        and 1 <= next_n <= 4
+        and has_litetopk_decode()
+    )
+
+
+def litetopk_select(scores, lengths, histogram, output, workspace) -> None:
+    """Write logical indices, ordered by score then lower logical index on ties.
+
+    Output order is unspecified. Short rows are padded with -1. Histogram and
+    workspace must belong exclusively to this stream until selection finishes.
+    """
+    torch.ops._C.litetopk_decode(
+        scores, lengths, histogram, output, workspace, CANDIDATE_CAPACITY
+    )
